\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{فلسفة} (falsafa)}{فلسفة (falsafa)}]{\ar{فلسفة} (falsafa) — philosophy}

\label{lesson:AR-C376-falsafa}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for likewise, then the Arabic for moreover.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{فلسفة}}
\textbf{\ar{فلسفة}} — \emph{falsafa} — \textquotedblleft{}philosophy\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{يدرس} \ar{ابن} \ar{عمي} \ar{الفلسفة} \ar{في} \ar{الجامعة}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{yadrusu ibn ʿammī al-falsafa fī al-jāmiʿa.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My cousin studies philosophy at university.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{فلسفة}} (\emph{falsafa}) was borrowed from Greek \emph{philosophia}, \textquotedblleft{}love of wisdom\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB). Arabic fitted the loan to its own four-consonant pattern.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{falsafa}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{falsafa}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{yadrusu ibn ʿammī al-falsafa fī al-jāmiʿa.} — My cousin studies philosophy at university.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for likewise, then the Arabic for moreover, then say \emph{falsafa} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{فلسفة} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Philosophy\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{لغويات} (lughawiyyāt)}{لغويات (lughawiyyāt)}]{\ar{لغويات} (lughawiyyāt) — linguistics}

\label{lesson:AR-C376-lughawiyyat}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for moreover, then the Arabic for philosophy.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{لغويات}}
\textbf{\ar{لغويات}} — \emph{lughawiyyāt} — \textquotedblleft{}linguistics\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{تخصصت} \ar{أختي} \ar{في} \ar{اللغويات}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{takhaṣṣaṣat ukhtī fī al-lughawiyyāt.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My sister specialized in linguistics.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{لغويات}} (\emph{lughawiyyāt}) is a modern plural built on \emph{lugha}, \textquotedblleft{}a language\textquotedblright{}, which Lane files under the native Arabic root \emph{l-gh-w} (Lane). It names the study of language.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{فيلسوف} (faylasūf)}{فيلسوف (faylasūf)}]{\ar{فيلسوف} (faylasūf) — a philosopher}

\label{lesson:AR-C376-faylasuf}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for philosophy, then the Arabic for linguistics.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{فيلسوف}}
\textbf{\ar{فيلسوف}} — \emph{faylasūf} — \textquotedblleft{}a philosopher\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{قرأت} \ar{كتابا} \ar{لفيلسوف} \ar{قديم}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{qaraʾtu kitāban li-faylasūf qadīm.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
I read a book by an ancient philosopher.
\end{quote}

Plural \ar{فلاسفة}, \emph{falāsifa}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{فيلسوف}} (\emph{faylasūf}) was borrowed from Greek \emph{philosophos}, \textquotedblleft{}a lover of wisdom\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB). Its sister word is \emph{falsafa}, philosophy.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{خبير} (khabīr)}{خبير (khabīr)}]{\ar{خبير} (khabīr) — an expert}

\label{lesson:AR-C376-khabir}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for linguistics, then the Arabic for a philosopher.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{خبير}}
\textbf{\ar{خبير}} — \emph{khabīr} — \textquotedblleft{}an expert\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{سأل} \ar{الصحفي} \ar{خبيرا} \ar{في} \ar{التاريخ}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{saʾala aṣ-ṣaḥafī khabīran fī at-tārīkh.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The journalist asked an expert on history.
\end{quote}

Plural: \ar{خبراء}, \emph{khubarāʾ}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{خبير}} (\emph{khabīr}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{kh-b-r}, \textquotedblleft{}to know thoroughly, to test\textquotedblright{} (Lane). A \emph{khabīr} knows a thing from the inside: an expert.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{أكاديمي} (akādīmī)}{أكاديمي (akādīmī)}]{\ar{أكاديمي} (akādīmī) — academic}

\label{lesson:AR-C376-akadimi}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for a philosopher, then the Arabic for an expert.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{أكاديمي}}
\textbf{\ar{أكاديمي}} — \emph{akādīmī} — \textquotedblleft{}academic\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{يعمل} \ar{عمي} \ar{في} \ar{مجال} \ar{أكاديمي}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{yaʿmalu ʿammī fī majāl akādīmī.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My uncle works in an academic field.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{أكاديمي}} (\emph{akādīmī}) is a modern loan with the Arabic ending \emph{-ī}. It is usually traced to Greek \emph{akadēmia}, the name of a school of learning, through European languages.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}
